messages:
alex: Hey team — customer sees duplicate POSTs and double billing when our SDK retries after a timeout. Happened 3 times today, intermittent. Request id: x-req-9982. Repro attached below.

sam: Oof. Which SDK + undici + node versions? Any proxy or gateway in front?

alex: SDK@0.7.2, undici@5.16.0, node v18.18.0. No special proxy on our side (customer sits behind a CDN). Minimal repro:
```js
const ac = new AbortController();
setTimeout(() => ac.abort(), 1200);
await fetch(url, {
  method: 'POST',
  body: fs.createReadStream('/path/to/file'), // streaming body in customer's app
  signal: ac.signal
});
```
We rely on SDK automatic retries: retries: 3, baseDelayMs: 300. Their logs show server received two separate uploads and charged twice.

maria: Streaming body explains it. If the body is a non-rewindable stream (fs.createReadStream) a retry will re-send from the start only if the SDK clones the stream — which generally isn't possible. With undici there've been edge cases where aborted requests still flushed bytes to the socket and retries caused duplicate deliveries.

pj: Short-term mitigations:
- Ask customer to switch to a buffer-backed body when possible (Buffer.from or read into memory) so fetch can resend.
- Disable automatic retries for endpoints that accept non-idempotent stream uploads. Eg: sdkClient.request({..., retry: {maxRetries: 0}}) or our internal flag to detect non-clonable body.
- Implement an idempotency key on uploads (preferred for production).

sam: Can you paste the relevant logs? Need the SDK request ids + our server trace ids to correlate. Also try bumping undici to 5.17.x in a quick test — there was a small fix around signal handling.

alex: Logs from customer sanitized: 
[1749876543] SDK -> POST /upload reqid=ae3f.. status=timeout aborted after 1200ms (client abort)
[1749876550] SDK retry -> POST /upload reqid=ae3f-retry1 status=200 server-accept tid=srv-42b
[1749876552] SDK retry -> POST /upload reqid=ae3f-retry2 status=200 server-accept tid=srv-42c
Customer says they got two charges and both server traces show distinct multipart boundaries and file sizes matched — so server accepted two full uploads.

maria: Filed internal bug INFR-512 to track: "retries with non-rewindable bodies can produce duplicate delivery when abort races with socket flush". Repro notes: fs.createReadStream + AbortController.abort() triggered after headers sent but before full body written. Undici sometimes lets remaining body bytes hit socket instead of interrupting.

support-bot: Created support ticket TKT-8347 and linked to INFR-512. Customer notified and given temporary workaround (disable retries or use idempotency key).

pj: Proposed quick patch: detect Body stream that has no .clone or is not a Buffer/string and auto-disable retries in SDK with a warning. I'll open a PR tomorrow to add config `skipRetriesIfStreamBody: true` + docs.

sam: Good. Also ask customer to try undici@5.17.0 + SDK canary to see if still reproduces. If they can give us a tiny repro repo (streams + abort) we can run locally.

alex: I'll ask for a minimal repro (preferably dockerized). Looping customer in and recommending idempotency keys for uploads. Thanks all :thumbsup:
